Answer: B
Reason: The chest radiograph demonstrates a large, thin-walled cystic cavity with an air-fluid level in the left lower lobe (retrocardiac region), which is a classic presentation of infected intralobar pulmonary sequestration. This finding aligns with the typical location and radiographic appearance of this congenital malformation, distinguishing it from the other options describing different lobes or pathologies.
